Polygonize a raster, by cell or by value

Source: R/polygonize.R
polygonize_raster.Rd

Turns the cells of a one-layer raster that have a value into polygons holding that value. By default each cell becomes its own square polygon, such as the planning-unit polygons of an AOI raster from rasterize_aoi(): neighbouring cells with the same value stay separate polygons, so every cell keeps its own row. With dissolve = TRUE, all cells with the same value are merged into one feature, such as one feature per class of a classified raster.

Usage

polygonize_raster(x, value = names(x), id = NULL, dissolve = FALSE)

Arguments

x

The raster: a SpatRaster with one layer, or a path to a raster file with one layer.

value

The name of the column that holds the raster value: a single, non-empty string. Defaults to the layer's name ("index" for the default output of rasterize_aoi()). wtw-data-prep2 uses "NCCID".

id

NULL (the default) or the name of a column to add that numbers the rows 1 to n in their order (see "Method"): a single, non-empty string, different from value. wtw-data-prep2 uses "PUID".

dissolve

FALSE (the default) for one polygon per cell, or TRUE for one feature per distinct value, merging all cells with that value (see "Method").

Value

An sf data frame in the raster's CRS: with dissolve = FALSE, one POLYGON row per cell that has a value; with dissolve = TRUE, one POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON row per distinct value. Its columns are value (the raster value, an integer or a double as the raster stores it), then id (an integer, 1 to n) if given, then geometry. A raster with no values gives zero rows. Nothing is written.

Method

  • Polygons (dissolve = FALSE, the default): terra::as.polygons() with dissolve = FALSE. Each cell that is not NA becomes one square polygon whose corners are the cell's corners (a ring of four corners, closed), so polygons share edges exactly with their neighbours. Neighbouring cells with equal values are not merged. Cells that are NA get no polygon.

  • Order (dissolve = FALSE): terra's cell order, row by row from the top-left cell, so id 1 is the first cell with a value in the top row that has one. The order does not depend on the values.

  • Merged polygons (dissolve = TRUE): one feature per distinct value, holding every cell with that value, whether or not the cells touch. The distinct values are found exactly (no rounding) and numbered 1 to n in ascending order, and the raster of those numbers is polygonized with terra::as.polygons() (dissolve = TRUE). So values that differ only slightly are never merged, as they could be with terra's own dissolve = TRUE, which rounds values and compares them in single precision. Edges shared by cells of the same value are removed. A value in one connected patch gives a POLYGON (with holes where it encloses other cells); a value in several separate patches gives one MULTIPOLYGON, so the geometry column can mix the two types. Each feature's area is its number of cells times the cell area. Cells that are NA get no polygon. One feature per connected patch, rather than per value, is not offered.

  • Order (dissolve = TRUE): by value, ascending, so id numbers the values 1 to n, not the cells.

  • Values: the raster's values, not rounded, in the type the raster stores (ADR 0019): an integer column if the raster stores integers (terra::is.int(): an INT* data type on file, such as NAT_DATA's idx.tif, or integer values in memory, such as the cell numbers of rasterize_aoi()), and a double column if it stores floats, even when the values are whole numbers. Integers outside R's integer range (possible only with INT4U or larger types) stay doubles. Files written from the result keep the type, so a shapefile gets an integer field.

  • CRS: the raster's; nothing is reprojected and no areas are computed.

With dissolve = FALSE, every cell with a value becomes a polygon, so polygonizing a large raster (such as the whole national template) makes millions of polygons; crop the raster to the area first, as rasterize_aoi() does by default.

See also

rasterize_aoi() makes the AOI rasters this function is used on.

Other raster: align_raster(), write_raster_file(), write_rasters()

Examples

template <- system.file("extdata", "template.tif", package = "constechr")
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")
x <- rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "touches")

# One polygon per cell, holding its template cell number in "index"
polygonize_raster(x)
#> Simple feature collection with 9 features and 1 field
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003000 ymin: 604000 xmax: 1006000 ymax: 607000
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>   index                       geometry
#> 1    34 POLYGON ((1003000 606000, 1...
#> 2    35 POLYGON ((1004000 606000, 1...
#> 3    36 POLYGON ((1005000 606000, 1...
#> 4    44 POLYGON ((1003000 605000, 1...
#> 5    45 POLYGON ((1004000 605000, 1...
#> 6    46 POLYGON ((1005000 605000, 1...
#> 7    54 POLYGON ((1003000 604000, 1...
#> 8    55 POLYGON ((1004000 604000, 1...
#> 9    56 POLYGON ((1005000 604000, 1...

# wtw-data-prep2's column names, with planning units numbered 1 to n
pu <- polygonize_raster(x, value = "NCCID", id = "PUID")
pu
#> Simple feature collection with 9 features and 2 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003000 ymin: 604000 xmax: 1006000 ymax: 607000
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>   NCCID PUID                       geometry
#> 1    34    1 POLYGON ((1003000 606000, 1...
#> 2    35    2 POLYGON ((1004000 606000, 1...
#> 3    36    3 POLYGON ((1005000 606000, 1...
#> 4    44    4 POLYGON ((1003000 605000, 1...
#> 5    45    5 POLYGON ((1004000 605000, 1...
#> 6    46    6 POLYGON ((1005000 605000, 1...
#> 7    54    7 POLYGON ((1003000 604000, 1...
#> 8    55    8 POLYGON ((1004000 604000, 1...
#> 9    56    9 POLYGON ((1005000 604000, 1...

# Equal values are not merged: nine cells of 1 give nine polygons
ones <- rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "touches", value = 1)
nrow(polygonize_raster(ones))
#> [1] 9

# dissolve = TRUE merges cells by value: here, one feature per class of
# the template's cell numbers grouped into tens
classes <- terra::rast(template) %/% 10
polygonize_raster(classes, value = "class", id = "id", dissolve = TRUE)
#> Simple feature collection with 11 features and 2 fields
#> Geometry type: GEOMETRY
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1e+06 ymin: 6e+05 xmax: 1010000 ymax: 610000
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> First 10 features:
#>    class id                       geometry
#> 1      0  1 POLYGON ((1002000 610000, 1...
#> 2      1  2 MULTIPOLYGON (((1009000 610...
#> 3      2  3 MULTIPOLYGON (((1009000 609...
#> 4      3  4 MULTIPOLYGON (((1009000 608...
#> 5      4  5 MULTIPOLYGON (((1009000 607...
#> 6      5  6 MULTIPOLYGON (((1009000 606...
#> 7      6  7 MULTIPOLYGON (((1009000 605...
#> 8      7  8 MULTIPOLYGON (((1009000 604...
#> 9      8  9 MULTIPOLYGON (((1009000 603...
#> 10     9 10 MULTIPOLYGON (((1009000 602...
